artifacts.summary: Eight-phase plan adding an append-only detected_defects observation log to both /orchestrate engines: accumulator declaration in mt_state_file and .orchestrator-loop-guard, wiring of all 11 detection sites (including the skill-base.sh site via a caller-side discriminant), postflight metadata propagation, a net-new hard-mode Stage 8 metadata merge, and enumerated rendering in commands/orchestrate.md.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, skill-orchestrate and skill-orchestrate-hard are NOT a wrapper pair: hard mode has no multi-task (MT-1..MT-5) implementation of its own and delegates entirely to base's MT stages, while its single-task stages (2, 5, 8) are a structurally separate reimplementation. The practical planning rule: a change to any MT stage is wired once in skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and automatically covers /orchestrate --hard batches; a change to any single-task stage MUST be mirrored in both files or it silently applies to only one engine (a named recurring defect class in this codebase). The two single-task paths have also drifted structurally -- e.g. base's Stage 8 carries a .return-meta.json metadata merge that hard's Stage 8 lacks entirely, and base's skill_gate_completion_claim call has no else branch while hard's does -- so a mirrored edit is rarely a verbatim copy and needs a per-file anchor check before editing. A parity audit phase that counts new tokens per file is the cheap guard.
